MN DNR site 235 is a live Stillwater gauge on the lower St. Croix, with official public-access and water-trail context. It is route-capable, but no distinct PaddleToday scored route is tied directly to this gauge in the current inventory, and the reviewed sources provide a boating/no-wake high-water rule rather than a route-specific paddling threshold and complete endpoint package for a new reach.
blockers: No distinct public point-to-point route reach tied directly to Stillwater site 235 was found beyond existing lower St. Croix coverage and access context.
The reviewed official Stillwater material supplies a 683.0 ft no-wake rule and boating hazards, not a route-specific paddling threshold ladder for a new scored card.
A new route would still require named endpoint pair, endpoint coordinates, camping/no-camping handling, safety package, image decision, and canonical geometry.
evidence: https://www.dnr.state.mn.us/river_levels/index.html identifies Minnesota DNR state-water-trail gauges and explains that interpretations are based on paddler and staff experience.

MN DNR site 239 is a live St. Louis River discharge gauge at Scanlon, and the official St. Louis State Water Trail map places the gauge at river mile 33.0 beside Scanlon carry-in access. It is route-capable, but the reach is dominated by Scanlon Dam, Thomson Reservoir, and Class IV-V/VI expert whitewater, while the reviewed sources do not provide a product-ready route-specific threshold ladder and complete endpoint package for a safe scored route.
blockers: The official map identifies Scanlon Dam at river mile 33.7 with no portage and Thomson Dam at river mile 29.7; the intervening reach carries expert-only Class IV-V whitewater and sharp-rock hazards.
No route-specific numeric paddling threshold tied to site 239, suitable routeType/skill handling, or complete endpoint/camping/coordinate/image/geometry package cleared the scored-route gate.
Any future implementation would require a deliberate expert-whitewater product decision and manager-backed hazard/portage treatment rather than a standard day-route card.
evidence: https://www.dnr.state.mn.us/climate/waterlevels/streams/stlouis.html identifies the St. Louis River at Scanlon gauge.
https://www.dnr.state.mn.us/state-water-trails/st-louis-river/segments-maps.html identifies the Scanlon-to-Thomson corridor, expert-only rapids, dams, and the St. Louis National Water Trail context.

https://files.dnr.state.mn.us/maps/canoe_routes/stlouis3.pdf places Scanlon carry-in access at RM 33.3, the river-level gauge at RM 33.0, Scanlon Dam at RM 33.7, Thomson Dam at RM 29.7, and warns of Class IV-V rapids and no portage.

MN DNR gauge 27 is directly relevant to the published Island Lake Dam-to-Bachelor Road Cloquet route because Island Lake Dam releases control the reach. reviews.decisionReason: Fresh review found the official Minnesota DNR river-level feed provides a station-specific rating ladder for gauge 284: rating 5 below 9.0 ft, rating 4 from 9.0 to 9.5 ft, rating 3 from 9.5 to 13.0 ft, rating 2 from 13.0 to 14.0 ft, and rating 1 above 14.0 ft. The gauge is at river mile 52.8 inside the already published Two Rivers to Dundas corridor, so this evidence supports a direct-gauge integration review but not a distinct new route. Keep the gauge blocked for coverage until the existing route is deliberately migrated; do not add a duplicate.
blockers: DNR 284 provides gage height only; no route-specific discharge or interpreted threshold band is available.
Existing upper-Cannon route package uses the direct Northfield discharge gauge; proxy coverage does not satisfy covered-state policy.

Minnesota DNR site 340 is the Straight River at Owatonna, Bridge Street, and the official Straight/Cannon water-trail map places a river-level gauge at Bridge Street on the canoeable corridor. The gauge is therefore route-capable, but the current scored route packages use the downstream Faribault interpreted gauge (site 247) and do not yet provide a separate Owatonna-to-Medford route package with its own endpoint, threshold, geometry, and safety evidence. Keep this gauge in the blocked lane rather than inventing a second route solely to increase gauge coverage.
blockers: No current scored route directly uses the Owatonna Bridge Street gauge; existing route cards use the downstream Faribault site 247 as direct or conservative proxy evidence.

A new Owatonna reach would require a defensible public endpoint pair, route geometry, route-specific numeric interpretation, and a complete safety/access package; the DNR map alone is not enough to create that card.
The DNR description identifies seasonal low water, dams, fast/narrow channel, and a Class II-III Clinton Falls portage, so a route cannot be promoted without explicitly handling those hazards.
evidence: https://www.dnr.state.mn.us/state-water-trails/straight-river/index.html identifies the Straight River as a 34-mile state water trail from south of Owatonna to Faribault.
https://www.dnr.state.mn.us/state-water-trails/straight-river/segments-maps.html documents the 30-80 foot, 1-4 foot channel, seasonal low-water limitation, dams, and hazards.
https://files.dnr.state.mn.us/maps/canoe_routes/cannon1_straight.pdf marks the Owatonna Bridge Street river-level gauge and public access/portage sequence on the official map.
https://www.dnr.state.mn.us/river_levels/index.html is the official DNR interpreted river-level source used by the existing Straight River route cards.

Bounded official-source screen refreshed the South Fork Crow corridor. DNR confirms the Little Kandiyohi-to-Cosmos reach is channelized, narrow, and subject to low flows; its only recommended day trip is Watertown-to-Lake Rebecca, downstream of gauge 53. Current DNR gauge data and named water-trail hazards do not establish a distinct Cosmos route package or threshold. Preserve as explicit blocked opportunity.
blockers: No source-backed numeric paddling threshold tied to MN DNR gauge 53 was validated; a current reading alone is not a paddleability threshold.
DNR describes Little Kandiyohi-to-Cosmos as channelized, narrow, and subject to low flows; its named recommended day trip begins below the Watertown dam and ends at Lake Rebecca, not at Cosmos.
DNR documents dams, logjams, overhanging trees, and submerged snags, while a distinct Cosmos endpoint, camping/no-camping, coordinate, image, and canonical geometry package remains incomplete.

reviews.decisionReason: Fresh bounded screen kept MN DNR site 54 blocked: current DNR telemetry is 262 cfs in rating band 3 at river mile 19.6 with a defensible gauge coordinate, and the current South Fork Crow State Water Trail map names the Mayer-area CR30, CR23, and Highway 7 bridges. However, it does not identify a public launch/parking facility at those Mayer bridges; the named DNR recommended route remains the distinct Rick Johnson Park-to-Lake Rebecca reach downstream. No Mayer endpoint access package, route-specific threshold, camping, image, or canonical geometry cleared publication.
blockers: DNR names CR30, CR23, and Highway 7 bridges near Mayer but does not document a public paddling put-in/parking facility at those bridges; no launch pair can be inferred.
The named DNR recommended route is Rick Johnson Park (river mile 13.8) to Lake Rebecca (river mile 24.7), a distinct downstream reach; the Mayer segment lacks its own route package.
Current DNR rating band 3 is live telemetry context, not a route-specific paddling threshold for the Mayer segment.
Mayer camping terms, rights-clean image selection, and canonical route geometry remain unverified.

The DNR route package documents named launches elsewhere and existing scored Kettle routes cover the documented public-access corridor; CR12 remains a gauge-only bridge point with no lawful distinct endpoint pair.
blockers: County Road 12 bridge is documented as a gauge point, not a public water access; do not infer launch rights from the bridge.
Existing scored Kettle routes cover the DNR-documented public-access corridor, including the recommended Musclewood-to-#1 and #5-to-#6 sections.
Current reading/rating is gauge context and the DNR Medium-or-above rule is not a new CR12-specific route threshold.
A distinct route would require new lawful endpoint/access, camping, image, coordinate, and geometry evidence.

reviews.decisionReason: The South Fork Shenandoah is a named public paddling corridor and USGS 01628500 supplies current direct telemetry near Lynnwood, but the bounded review did not find an exact public endpoint pair with route-specific runnable thresholds explicitly tied to this gauge. Preserve the opportunity without inferring a route or threshold.

Verify route distance, access, safety, and threshold applicability without borrowing downstream gauge guidance.

reviews.decisionReason: The published Newport-to-White House Landing route is an exact named public corridor directly represented by USGS 01629500. Virginia DWR confirms both access points, American Whitewater supplies the encompassing Class I-II reach and 450-2,500 cfs correlation, and the route passes evidence, safety, coordinate, geometry, test, build, verification, and rollback gates.

American Whitewater directly correlates its Class I-II Bixler's Bridge-to-Bentonville reach to USGS 01631000 at 1.25-3.8 ft, and DWR lists multiple current public South Fork accesses. blockers: Select an exact current DWR endpoint pair wholly inside the AW reach and verify its river distance.
Confirm that the 1.25-3.8 ft AW correlation applies to that exact subroute rather than inferring from a downstream anecdotal minimum.

Preserve the reservoir as recreational access, but do not force a scored flow route from this gauge.
blockers: officially supported paddling is reservoir recreation rather than a point-to-point flow-responsive river corridor
Woodburn Road ramp is permanently closed and Woodlands Road has very limited parking
below-dam mainstem Rivanna routes require their own gauge relationship and route-specific threshold package

reviews.decisionReason: USGS 02032640 is a fresh direct gauge for American Whitewater's named North Fork Rivanna corridor from Advance Mills to US 29. The current screen did not establish either road crossing as a maintained public launch, and Virginia DWR's current access inventory has no North Fork site. Two dam portages remain unresolved, including one described as an unsafe ladder or likely trespass, the source disagrees on reach distance, and trip reports conflict materially on minimum stage. No safe exact public corridor and defensible threshold package cleared, so no route was published.
blockers: Advance Mills and US 29 are not established as a current public launch and takeout pair
two dam portages lack a manager-confirmed lawful and safe portage package
the reach source conflicts on distance and reports materially conflicting minimum-stage guidance
current reports include river-wide wood and steep-bank hazards

reviews.decisionReason: At least one scored route uses this gauge directly.

USGS 02035000 is fresh direct telemetry beside DWR's Cartersville launch. Virginia DWR documents an exact 5-mile Cartersville-to-West View float, Goochland County lists both launches and a 2-3 hour canoe time, and the current DWR access dataset confirms both are DWR-owned concrete ramps. The screen found flood-stage and historical hydrology values but no source-backed paddling minimum, maximum, or conservative route-specific rule for this exact float. Hydrologic extremes are not recreational thresholds, so no scored route was published.
blockers: no source-backed numeric paddling minimum, maximum, or conservative station rule tied to Cartersville-to-West View
USGS low-flow statistics and NWS flood stages describe hydrology and flood risk but do not establish recreational suitability

reviews.decisionReason: USGS 02036500 is a fresh discharge-and-stage station on a 22.4-square-mile Fine Creek basin, but the bounded route-first and gauge-assisted screen found no named paddling corridor, no public Fine Creek endpoint pair, no DWR-maintained Fine Creek access, and no paddling threshold evidence. Current Powhatan recreation and Middle James planning sources identify nearby James River canoe access and the Fine Creek Mills historic district, not a Fine Creek water trail. This gauge is not a supported scored-route opportunity on current evidence.
blockers: no named paddling corridor or public endpoint pair
no DWR-maintained Fine Creek boating access

reviews.decisionReason: USGS 0203668750 is fresh stage telemetry on Tuckahoe Creek, but Henrico County's current Tuckahoe Creek Park page expressly prohibits boating and swimming. The county master plan depicts a future Wilton Landing paddle-launch concept, not a verified open public endpoint, and the bounded screen found no current named point-to-point corridor or station-specific numeric paddling guidance. Do not convert a future concept or prohibited park reach into a scored route.
blockers: current Tuckahoe Creek Park rules prohibit boating
Wilton Landing paddle access is a plan concept rather than a verified open public endpoint
no named point-to-point corridor or station-specific numeric paddling guidance

reviews.decisionReason: At least one scored route uses this gauge directly.

USGS 0203755233 is stage-only telemetry on Little Westham Creek inside the University of Richmond campus. The university documents a restored eco-corridor, ADA trail, stream habitat, and education use rather than a public paddling corridor. The creek does not provide a supported endpoint pair or route-specific numeric guidance, so it is not a defensible scored-route opportunity on current evidence.
blockers: officially documented use is an urban stream eco-corridor and trail rather than paddling
stage-only station has no route-specific numeric paddling guidance

reviews.decisionReason: USGS 02037724 is an unnamed tributary at Oakleys Lane with stage-only telemetry and no named public paddling corridor or point-to-point endpoint pair. Virginia DWR's maintained boating-access inventory identifies public launches on the James River and other named waters, while the Richmond-area Four Mile Creek recreation evidence is a separate named waterway; no authoritative recreational route package was found for this unnamed tributary.
blockers: unnamed tributary with no named public paddle corridor
no public point-to-point endpoint pair or route-specific paddling evidence
stage-only telemetry has no product-supported route threshold

reviews.decisionReason: Four Mile Creek is a genuine named recreational waterway: Henrico County describes canoe and guided flatwater paddles up the creek from Deep Bottom Park, and DWR confirms Deep Bottom as a public two-ramp access on the tidal James. However, USGS 02038730 is stage-only, has a 3.99-square-mile basin, and no station-specific paddling threshold or manager-published point-to-point route with a distinct takeout was verified. Preserve as a route-capable candidate rather than infer a threshold from the James gauge or create an out-and-back route.
blockers: stage-only station has no station-specific recreational threshold
named recreation is documented but no manager-published point-to-point endpoint pair and takeout were verified
access, safety, camping/no-camping, coordinate, image, and canonical geometry package remains incomplete

reviews.decisionReason: USGS 0203873175 is a direct Four Mile Creek stage-only station near Kingsland Road. Current Henrico materials document guided canoe and SUP use on Four Mile Creek from Deep Bottom Park, and DWR confirms the nearby Deep Bottom public access, but no station-specific runnable threshold, named point-to-point corridor, or distinct public takeout was verified. Do not transfer James River thresholds or treat a calm guided paddle as a scored route without a complete route package.
blockers: stage-only station has no station-specific recreational threshold
no distinct manager-published point-to-point endpoint pair and takeout tied to this station
access, safety, camping/no-camping, coordinate, image, and canonical geometry package remains incomplete

Preserve blocked until a public-access owner/source confirms endpoint rights and current portage/safety conditions.

reviews.decisionReason: The official Upper Shenango Water Trail and Shenango River Watchers publish a strong 21-mile corridor with named public launches, including Golden Run, Clark, Shenango, Mahaney, and Hartford. USGS 03103500 has current discharge and stage telemetry. Publication remains blocked because the published 4.6-5.6 ft recommendation is tied to the Pymatuning Dam gauge rather than 03103500, the launch-pair geometry and current closure/portage status are not yet verified, and rights-clean route imagery has not been selected.

USGS 03104490 has stage and temperature history but no current discharge series suitable for the product live-gauge requirement. The site is downstream on the same Shenango system as the Upper Shenango opportunity, while authoritative water-trail sources do not establish a distinct route package for this gauge. Screen out rather than create a duplicate stage-only route.
No complete route evidence package was established in the bounded review; preserve as an explicit blocked opportunity rather than force a route.

Connoquenessing Creek has a documented 6.4-mile RR-bridge-to-Rock-Point reach with gauge-linked stage guidance and public launch names, but the bounded review did not establish authoritative endpoint coordinates and exact station-to-reach mapping. Preserve as an explicit blocked opportunity rather than force a route.

reviews.decisionReason: No-add after bounded research: USGS provides direct discharge and stage telemetry near Portersville, but the station is on the Muddy Creek tributary feeding Lake Arthur. Moraine sources document lake boating and park launches, not a distinct station-gauged creek route; no named public launch/takeout pair or station-specific runnable threshold was found for the creek.

Raccoon Creek has three named canoe-guide reaches tied to USGS 03108000 with stage guidance, but the bounded review did not establish a public, coordinate-backed endpoint pair for a complete reach. Preserve as an explicit blocked opportunity rather than force a route.

reviews.decisionReason: USGS observations end 2025-10-18, so the station is not currently supported as a live product gauge. Montgomery Locks and Dam has restricted shoreline access, a 300-foot downstream boating restriction, and commercial navigation hazards; no safe endpoint pair or station-specific paddling threshold was established.

Live stage telemetry and a distinct Montgomery navigation-pool station are supported, but the closest formal public access is downstream at Kilbuck and the lock area has heavy commercial traffic and restrictions. reviews.decisionReason: The gauge has a usable live USGS feed and local flow references (about 200 cfs as a low-water observation; Morgan's stops rentals over 4.5 ft), and the Whitewater corridor is distinct. A publishable route still lacks a fully current pair of named public launch/take-out endpoints: Laurel access is documented as public, but downstream access descriptions are dated, fee-based, or informal, and the 28.4-mile scenic segment includes feeder-dam and private-bank hazards. Durable no-add until endpoint status and route geometry are independently verified.
blockers: current public take-out endpoint not verified for a distinct route
Laurel Feeder Dam and downstream low-head/dam hazards require explicit portage treatment

reviews.decisionReason: The USGS station is Eagle Creek at 79th Street and provides stage-only telemetry. Search results for a 79th Street canoe route refer to the separate Fall Creek Canoe Trail, while Eagle Creek Park access is reservoir access at 56th/71st Street and the marina. No distinct named public paddle corridor tied to this Eagle Creek gauge was verified; preserve durable no-add and do not conflate the waterways.
blockers: stage-only gauge with no discharge threshold
79th Street route sources refer to Fall Creek, not Eagle Creek
no distinct Eagle Creek gauge-linked public endpoint pair
access, safety, camping, geometry, and rights-clean image package incomplete

reviews.decisionReason: Durable no-add after bounded research: USGS identifies 03353415 as the upstream School Branch at Maloney Road monitoring point, part of the same small School Branch water-quality study as 03353420. No named public paddle endpoints or distinct route corridor were found, and the official research is about discharge, nutrient, sediment, turbidity, and agricultural water-quality conditions rather than recreation. No station-specific paddling threshold or safe-flow guidance exists. Do not create a route from telemetry alone.
blockers: no named public paddle endpoint pair or route corridor
no station-specific paddling threshold or safe-flow guidance
water-quality monitoring context is not evidence of recreational suitability

DNR warns the Skibo Mills to Highway 100 upper St. Louis boulder-bed corridor may be impassable at medium to low water levels.
No public manager/source package ties USGS 04015438 to a selected endpoint pair, numeric threshold model, legal camping/no-camping terms, endpoint coordinates, image decision, and route geometry.

reviews.decisionReason: USGS 04021520 is Stoney Brook at Pine Drive near Brookston, a tributary gauge rather than a selected St. Louis River water-trail reach. Same-run discharge was the USGS missing-value sentinel with a backwater qualifier, and no official point-to-point paddling corridor, thresholds, public endpoint pair, camping/no-camping terms, safety package, coordinates, image, or geometry surfaced for Stoney Brook.
blockers: The gauge is on Stoney Brook, not on an official selected St. Louis River day-route reach.
Same-run USGS discharge was -999999 with a backwater qualifier, so discharge is not usable for route scoring.
No public route package exists for a Stoney Brook point-to-point paddle with endpoints, thresholds, camping, safety, coordinates, image, and geometry.

reviews.decisionReason: The gauge is explicitly recorded as stale, inapplicable, or unavailable to the product.

USGS 04024000 is the provider-equivalent Scanlon gauge for MN DNR site 239. It has extensive live stream telemetry and the official DNR St. Louis map places the gauge beside Scanlon access, but the same Scanlon-to-Thomson reach remains expert whitewater with no-portage dams and no product-ready route-specific threshold and safety package.
blockers: Provider-equivalent MN DNR site 239 is blocked for the same Scanlon expert-whitewater/no-portage corridor.
No scored route cleared a route-specific numeric paddling threshold, endpoint, skill/routeType, camping, safety, image, or geometry package for this station.
Any future use requires explicit expert-whitewater handling and manager-backed dam/portage guidance.
evidence: https://waterdata.usgs.gov/monitoring-location/USGS-04024000/ identifies St. Louis River at Scanlon, MN with continuous, daily, and field data and coordinates 46.703511, -92.418378.
https://files.dnr.state.mn.us/maps/canoe_routes/stlouis3.pdf places Scanlon carry-in access and the river-level gauge beside Scanlon Dam and Thomson Reservoir, with Class IV-V hazards and no portage.

https://www.dnr.state.mn.us/state-water-trails/st-louis-river/segments-maps.html describes the same corridor as expert-only whitewater in many sections and warns of multiple dams and Class I-VI rapids.

reviews.decisionReason: Fast screen confirms a live direct USGS gauge and Wisconsin DNR canoe context, but the DNR's Nemadji Floodplain Forest description requires landowner permission for land access and only describes a 1.3-mile downstream reach. Superior's city map labels a Nemadji canoe launch and fishing accesses without a route-specific endpoint/landing package. No station-specific paddling threshold, turbidity/impairment treatment, Lake Superior confluence safety package, camping, coordinates, image, or geometry package cleared publication.
blockers: no station-specific public endpoint pair or permitted land-access package is verified for the gauge reach
no station-specific paddling threshold is accepted
turbidity impairment and Lake Superior confluence hazards require explicit safety treatment
camping, image, coordinate, and canonical geometry evidence remain incomplete

reviews.decisionReason: At least one scored route uses this gauge directly.

USGS 04026160 is a miscellaneous site with no continuous, daily, or field measurement data available, so it cannot provide a product-supported live gauge. Official Bayfield County and Lake Superior trail sources document coastal access and hazards, but the station cannot support a live-threshold route; no route added.

Whittlesey Creek has a live USGS station and public estuary/boat-landing evidence, but no station-tied upstream endpoint pair or validated paddling threshold package. The refuge prohibits camping, and coastal conditions are not interchangeable with the station corridor. No route added.
blockers: no station-tied upstream endpoint pair or station-specific paddling threshold
estuary/coastal evidence cannot substitute for the station corridor; refuge camping is prohibited
complete safety, coordinate, image, and geometry package is not validated

reviews.decisionReason: The Beartrap Creek station appears in historical USGS records, but current route-capable evidence is absent: no current PaddleToday-ready point-to-point corridor, public endpoints, threshold, access/camping, safety, coordinate, image, or geometry package was found. Treat the historical gauge as unsupported until current station and route evidence is refreshed.

Bounded review confirms no publishable route: USGS marks 04026511 discontinued for lack of funding, and no named public endpoints, route-specific threshold, or complete access/safety package cleared. Preserve as durable no-add until a supported replacement station and complete public route package exist.
blockers: USGS 04026511 is discontinued for lack of funding
no supported replacement live gauge or complete public route package

reviews.decisionReason: At least one scored route uses this gauge directly.

Bounded research confirmed that American Whitewater has gauge-matched Marengo reaches and named road endpoints, including a class II-III+ Town Hall Road-to-Four Corner Store Road run and a separate Snake Trail-to-Marengo Lake Road run with a 40-50 foot class V waterfall. However, the source calls the rating an educated guess, reports current flow below recommended, and does not establish manager-backed legal endpoint access or a conservative product threshold. The upper reach requires advanced whitewater and a difficult/uncertain waterfall portage; no safe family-facing scored route package cleared. No route was added.
blockers: American Whitewater's flow recommendation and class rating are not an authoritative station-specific threshold; current gauge is below recommended.
Public road names are documented, but legal manager-backed endpoint access and defensible arrival/parking coordinates are not validated.
Marengo Falls is a 40-50 foot class V hazard with uncertain/difficult portage; wood and narrow-channel hazards require advanced whitewater treatment.
Canonical geometry, camping/logistics, image rights, and duplicate/route-order evidence remain incomplete.

reviews.decisionReason: USGS identifies the Marengo River station but reports no continuous, daily, field-measurement, or statistical data, so the gauge is not currently usable for live route scoring.
blockers: USGS station currently has no available continuous, daily, field, or statistical data

reviews.decisionReason: Bounded research confirmed the direct Marengo River near Mellen gauge and a lower Government Road-to-Bad River canoe reach. American Whitewater explicitly flags access issues and requires permission from the Bad River Band for the downstream paddle-out; Wisconsin DNR describes the mouth entering the reservation and the reach's private/uncertain access context. The live gauge is available in legacy data, but no manager-backed legal endpoint pair, authoritative paddling threshold, shuttle/permission package, canonical geometry, camping, or rights-clean image decision cleared publication. No speculative route was added.
blockers: American Whitewater flags access issues and requires Bad River Band permission for the downstream paddle-out; legal endpoint access is unresolved.
No authoritative station-specific paddling threshold or complete live-gauge interpretation has cleared.
Shuttle/permission logistics, canonical geometry, camping, image rights, and duplicate/route-order evidence remain incomplete.

reviews.decisionReason: Fresh fast screen confirms the durable no-add. USGS current conditions show discharge and gage-height observations through 2026-08-08, but Iron County material describes Potato River Falls as a waterfall/campground context and the available evidence does not clear a safe bounded paddling reach. No PaddleToday-ready endpoint pair, station-specific operating threshold, portage/rapid safety package, or complete coordinate, camping, image, and geometry package is validated.
blockers: named public endpoint pair needs validation
waterfall/rapid and portage safety package not validated
camping, coordinate, image, and geometry package not validated

reviews.decisionReason: USGS 04073458 monitors the small Roy Creek tributary at Roy Creek Road near Green Lake. USGS reports a recent discharge of about 1.15 cfs, and the Green Lake paddling overview identifies public paddling on Green Lake, Silver Creek, and the Puchyan River rather than a Roy Creek point-to-point route. No authoritative Roy Creek endpoint pair, paddling thresholds, safety/camping package, or supported scored corridor was found.
blockers: No supported public Roy Creek point-to-point paddle corridor
Gauge is a small tributary and not the nearby Green Lake/Silver Creek/Puchyan route corridor
No route-quality package with endpoints, thresholds, safety, camping, coordinates, image, and geometry

reviews.decisionReason: Green Lake southwest inlet is a 15.7-square-mile inlet/water-quality station with no durable point-to-point paddle route tied to the gauge reach; nearby County K estuary access is shallow lake-estuary recreation rather than a supported scored river route.

USGS 04073462 is White Creek at Spring Grove Road near Green Lake, a 3.05-square-mile monitored tributary at a road culvert. The reviewed Green Lake paddling sources describe lake and larger connected-water recreation, but no public point-to-point White Creek paddle corridor or endpoint package. Its telemetry therefore does not establish route relevance for PaddleToday.
blockers: No supported public White Creek paddling corridor or endpoint pair found.
Green Lake paddling references concern the lake and larger connected waters, not this small tributary.
Telemetry at a road culvert is insufficient for route-capable coverage.

reviews.decisionReason: The review confirmed genuine public access at Spaulding Bridge Landing and a named Silver Creek Water Trail, plus a local 1.7-mile Spaulding Hill Road to Sunset Park segment. reviews.decisionReason: This is a strong distinct route opportunity: Northeast Indiana Water Trails publishes the approximately 5-mile Tonkel Road to State Road 1 reach with exact endpoint coordinates, public carry-down access, seasonal guidance, and fallen-tree/rapids caveats. The direct USGS 04180000 gauge is live and colocated on Cedar Creek, but no numeric paddling threshold or conservative station-specific go/no-go rule was found. Hold for threshold evidence rather than publish with an unsupported band.
blockers: no numeric paddling threshold or conservative station-specific go/no-go rule
seasonal low-water guidance is qualitative; fallen trees and small rapids require current field conditions

reviews.decisionReason: Durable no-add: Fort Wayne public sources identify Mayhew Road, Shoaff Park, Johnny Appleseed Park, and a distinct St. Joseph corridor, while USGS 04180500 has current discharge and stage telemetry. The only numeric or route-specific guidance found is an outdated Indiana canoe guide with private/changed access and no paddling threshold; no current station-specific recreational threshold supports a scored route.
blockers: no current station-specific numeric paddling threshold or conservative minimum-only rule
older route guide explicitly warns that access points changed and includes private access
current route-specific access, safety, camping, image, and geometry package is incomplete

reviews.decisionReason: Durable no-add: Fort Wayne water-trail sources provide named St. Joseph River endpoints, but USGS 04180610 has no continuous, daily, or field-measurement data and no current product-supported gauge signal. evidence.note: USGS lists continuous discharge and gage-height telemetry for Sand Hill River at Climax (05069000).

Current watershed guidance says flows at or below 40 cfs scrape bottom and flows over 200 cfs are fast with snag hazards; it references USGS at Climax and a DNR Fertile gauge but does not define a public Climax endpoint pair.
River Watch documents historical Climax-area reaches (US 75 to MN 220 and downstream) but flags snags, mud, and uncertain access; it is not current proof of a rights-clean route package.

reviews.decisionReason: The Red River is officially paddle-relevant, but the Thompson gauge has no station-specific public endpoint pair, gauge-tied paddling thresholds, camping terms, safety package, defensible route coordinates, rights-clean image decision, or canonical geometry for a scored reach.
blockers: No named public Thompson-area put-in/take-out pair was validated.
Minnesota DNR Red River guidance is generic and does not publish numeric private-paddlecraft bands tied to 05070000.
Camping/no-camping, safety, endpoint coordinates, image, and route geometry packages are not established.

reviews.decisionReason: Red Lake River is a state water trail, but the near-Red-Lake gauge sits in the headwater/reservation segment where DNR says paddling is prohibited unless a Red Lake Department of Natural Resources permit is obtained; same-run USGS discharge was backwater-affected and unusable. No route can be promoted without manager-grade permit/access, threshold, camping, safety, and coordinate evidence.
blockers: DNR Map 1 segment context says paddling from river mile 195.5 to 182.5 through the Red Lake Indian Reservation is prohibited unless a Red Lake DNR permit is obtained.
USGS discharge returned -999999 with a backwater qualifier, leaving stage-only telemetry.
No permit/access/camping/safety/coordinate route package was established for the gauge reach.

evidence.note: USGS Red Lake River near Red Lake returned discharge -999999 with P/Bkw qualifier and stage 69.73 ft at 2026-08-14 11:30 CDT.
Minnesota DNR identifies Red Lake River as a state water trail beginning at Upper and Lower Red Lake.
DNR Map 1 segment notes the first reach passes through the Red Lake Indian Reservation and paddling is prohibited unless a permit is obtained from Red Lake DNR.

reviews.decisionReason: The bounded review verified a distinct public-water-trail reach from High Landing (RM 163.4) to Smiley Bridge (RM 140.9), with a live USGS station at High Landing and DNR access/safety guidance. The opportunity remains blocked because no authoritative station-specific paddling threshold ladder or conservative minimum-only rule is published for USGS 05075000; historical flood-stage material is not a paddling qualification.
blockers: DNR documents High Landing and Smiley Bridge as public accesses on a distinct 22.5-mile reach, but no route-specific numeric paddling threshold ladder tied to USGS 05075000 was found.
Historical USGS/USACE flood-stage and discharge material is not sufficient to set a safe paddling threshold; do not convert it into a route recommendation.
The upstream Lower Red Lake Reservation restriction is avoided by the High Landing start, but must remain an explicit boundary in any future route package.

reviews.decisionReason: USGS 05076000 is live on the Thief River tributary, but no official Thief River state-water-trail or route-capable public point-to-point paddling package surfaced for this gauge reach.
blockers: No official Thief River paddling corridor or recommended point-to-point section surfaced.
No route-specific public endpoint pair, numeric thresholds, camping/no-camping terms, safety package, coordinates, image decision, or geometry package was found.
Nearby Red Lake River route evidence does not establish a Thief River route.

reviews.decisionReason: Clearwater River at Plummer has live discharge telemetry, but no official Minnesota state-water-trail segment or current PaddleToday-ready public endpoint package was found for this reach; telemetry alone does not establish route relevance.
blockers: No official water-trail segment or supported point-to-point paddling package surfaced.
No route-specific access, threshold, camping, and safety package was found.

reviews.decisionReason: Lost River at Oklee is a live USGS stream station, but Minnesota DNR water-trail materials do not identify a Lost River state-water-trail segment or a current point-to-point paddling package for this reach. Telemetry alone does not establish route relevance, so no scored route should be created from this gauge.
blockers: No official Minnesota state-water-trail segment or recommended paddling section surfaced for Lost River at Oklee.
No route-specific access, threshold, camping, and safety package was found.

reviews.decisionReason: USGS 05079000 is product-live in the Crookston Red Lake River corridor, but existing scored Crookston routes already use equivalent MN DNR site 172 with official thresholds; current coverage gates do not count cross-provider equivalents as covered.
blockers: Existing scored Crookston route coverage uses MN DNR site 172 rather than USGS 05079000.

reviews.decisionReason: USGS 05080000 is product-live in the Fisher Red Lake River corridor, but existing scored lower Red Lake routes already use equivalent MN DNR site 175 with official thresholds; current coverage gates do not count cross-provider equivalents as covered.
blockers: Existing scored Fisher route coverage uses MN DNR site 175 rather than USGS 05080000.

reviews.decisionReason: Grand Forks has public Red River access and broad paddling relevance, but no station-specific numeric threshold model and complete named endpoint package cleared for this direct gauge; existing Red River route family evidence does not justify a duplicate or inferred route.
blockers: No selected Grand Forks gauge-matched endpoint pair and route shape cleared for a new scored route.

reviews.decisionReason: Turtle River State Park materials document trails, a CCC dam, camping, and river views but do not identify a public point-to-point paddling corridor or named launch/take-out package for the Turtle River gauge reach.
blockers: No official/public point-to-point paddling corridor or endpoint pair surfaced.
The park's documented river infrastructure includes a CCC dam and trail crossings; no route-ready safety and portage package was established.
No route-specific threshold, coordinates, image, camping terms, or geometry package exists.

reviews.decisionReason: Bounded official-source screen confirmed that USGS 05083500 is stage-only and the DNR Red River Map 6 package is centered on the Drayton gauge and existing proxy coverage, without a distinct Oslo endpoint/threshold/camping/safety package. No route added; preserve as explicitly blocked until evidence changes.
blockers: No scored route is tied to USGS 05083500, and existing Map 6 coverage uses the upstream MN DNR Drayton gauge as a same-map proxy.
USGS 05083500 returned stage/elevation telemetry only in this run, with no discharge value for PaddleToday scoring.

DNR Map 6 provides Drayton-area accesses, a Drayton gauge, dam, and camping context, but no distinct Oslo-specific public endpoint pair, route distance, camping/no-camping terms, threshold ladder, safety package, or endpoint-coordinate package was accepted.

reviews.decisionReason: Forest River near Fordville has live telemetry and public wildlife/nature evidence, but reviewed official sources identify fishing, habitat, and nature-trail contexts rather than a public point-to-point paddling corridor with named legal endpoints.
blockers: No official/public Forest River paddling corridor or endpoint pair surfaced.
Wildlife and fishing access do not establish water-entry permission or a route-quality package.
No route-specific thresholds, camping, safety, coordinates, image, or geometry evidence exists.

reviews.decisionReason: Forest River at Minto belongs to the same unsupported Forest River family as the Fordville gauge; official material reviewed for the river identifies fishing, habitat, and general recreation but no public point-to-point paddling route package.
blockers: No distinct official/public Minto-area paddling corridor or named legal endpoint pair surfaced.
Fishing or wildlife access cannot be treated as water-entry permission.
No route-specific thresholds, camping, safety, coordinates, image, or geometry evidence exists.

reviews.decisionReason: USGS 05085450 is Snake River above Warren in the Red River basin, while Minnesota DNR's supported Snake River State Water Trail is a separate 84-mile corridor from McGrath to the St. Croix River. The station is not a gauge for the supported paddle corridor and no route package connects it to PaddleToday's published Snake routes.
blockers: Station is in the Red River basin and is not the Minnesota DNR Snake River State Water Trail gauge.
No supported point-to-point paddle route package was found for the Warren-area reach.

reviews.decisionReason: Middle River at Argyle is a live USGS stream station, and the river passes through Old Mill State Park, but Minnesota DNR water-trail and recommended-paddling materials do not identify a Middle River route or provide a complete point-to-point access, threshold, camping, and safety package. Telemetry alone is not sufficient for a scored route.
blockers: No official Minnesota state-water-trail segment or recommended paddling section surfaced for Middle River at Argyle.
Old Mill State Park presence does not establish a navigable point-to-point route or public endpoint package.
No route-specific access, threshold, camping, and safety package was found.

reviews.decisionReason: USGS 05089995 is the Park River diversion channel at Grafton, not a natural public point-to-point paddling reach. Current telemetry was 0.00 cfs / 23.99 ft at 2026-08-20 07:00 CDT, and North Dakota flood-control sources describe the diversion as a bypass channel, levee, and control-structure system. No supported recreational route should be inferred from flood-control infrastructure or telemetry.
blockers: The station is a flood-control diversion channel rather than a documented public paddling corridor.
No named public put-in/take-out pair, route threshold, camping/access, safety, image, coordinate, or geometry package surfaced.

reviews.decisionReason: USGS confirms a live Park River station at Grafton and Leistikow Park offers seasonal canoe/kayak rentals and camping. However, no manager-backed point-to-point access pair or station-specific paddling threshold was found. USGS also documents a separate diversion channel during high flow, so the main-channel gauge cannot be used to infer a route through adjacent channels. No complete route/safety/geometry package cleared.
blockers: Grafton Parks documents rental/campground context but not a selected public access-to-access river route.
No station-specific numeric paddling threshold or complete access, safety, image, coordinate, and geometry package surfaced.
USGS diversion-channel warning prevents substituting the adjacent channel or inferring route conditions from the main gauge.

reviews.decisionReason: USGS 05092000 is a product-live Red River gauge at Drayton, with 893 cfs / 11.56 ft at 2026-08-20 06:45 CDT. City of Drayton and the Minnesota DNR Map 5 identify Hastings Landing/Schumacher Park access and camping, and the DNR publishes Drayton stage bands, but the nearest documented upstream access is Oslo at river mile 274.5 versus Hastings at 209.2, a roughly 65-mile corridor rather than a safe PaddleToday day split. Existing Minnesota Red River cards use the Drayton DNR stage proxy; that proxy relationship does not make this USGS key covered.
blockers: Official access evidence does not provide a selected named day-route endpoint pair within the 05092000 reach; Oslo-to-Hastings is about 65 river miles.
The city requires a portage at Hastings to avoid Drayton Dam, and DNR warns of flooding, snags, low-water blockage, wind, and private shoreland.
Existing Golden Grain-to-Hilltop coverage uses an MN DNR Drayton proxy, so proxy/provider equivalence cannot be counted as direct USGS coverage.

reviews.decisionReason: USGS 05094000 is a live South Branch Two Rivers station at Lake Bronson, but the route evidence reviewed is lake/park and dam context rather than an official point-to-point river route. Lake Bronson materials document boating/canoeing around the impoundment and dam-created lake context, and current park material reports dam-replacement/lake-closure conditions. Under the river-route model this gauge is not paddle-relevant for a scored river route.
blockers: No official South Branch Two Rivers point-to-point river route package surfaced for the station reach.
Available public recreation evidence is Lake Bronson lake/park and dam context, not a scored river corridor.
Lake Bronson dam-replacement/lake-closure context blocks treating the lake setting as a current route substitute.

reviews.decisionReason: Bounded route-opportunity review confirmed a strong Little South Pembina corridor: American Whitewater ties the direct USGS 05099400 gauge to a 99th Street NE-to-123rd Avenue reach and reports approximately 100 cfs as an easier low-flow floor, while official North Dakota tourism sources confirm paddling access in the broader Pembina area. However, the specific bridge endpoints are not manager-backed for paddlers, the reach is a 5.6-19 mile family, and the threshold evidence is anecdotal rather than a defensible low/ideal/high model. No speculative route was added.
blockers: Selected 99th Street NE and 123rd Avenue bridge access is not cleanly manager-backed for paddlers.
The published reach is a 5.6-19 mile family rather than one unambiguous day route.
AW/community flow reports are not sufficient for a defensible low/ideal/high threshold; camping, safety, image, and canonical geometry remain incomplete.

reviews.decisionReason: At least one scored route uses this gauge directly.

USGS 05100000 is a product-live Pembina River gauge at Neche, but the bounded research sweep found no distinct Neche-area public endpoint pair or route package. Official North Dakota and Pembina County materials identify Vang Bridge, Brickmine Bridge, and Hwy 32/White Bridge as the supported Pembina access corridor, already covered by the 05099600 Walhalla route; the Neche gauge therefore cannot support a new scored route without station-tied thresholds, endpoints, safety, geometry, camping, and image evidence.
blockers: No named public Neche-area put-in/take-out pair or practical day-route distance was verified.
Existing Walhalla/Pembina Gorge threshold and access evidence is upstream and cannot be promoted as direct 05100000 coverage.
No route-specific camping, border/international-water safety, image, coordinate, or canonical geometry package cleared.

reviews.decisionReason: USGS 05101000 Tongue River at Akra has live discharge and stage, but the bounded North Dakota sweep found no official or public point-to-point paddling corridor or named endpoint package for this small Tongue River reach.
blockers: No official North Dakota water-trail or manager-backed public route package surfaced for Tongue River at Akra.
No named public endpoint pair, paddling threshold, camping, safety, coordinate, image, or geometry evidence exists for this reach.
Fresh telemetry is a hydrologic gauge context rather than evidence of a supported paddle corridor.

reviews.decisionReason: USGS 05102490 Red River of the North at Pembina has current stage-only provider support (10.80 ft at 2026-08-20 10:30 CDT) and no current discharge metric. The official Red River water trail supplies broad access, safety, and camping context, but this product cannot use the stage-only station as a supported live gauge for a new scored route.
blockers: Provider currently exposes gage height only; no discharge or accepted stage-only threshold is supported.
The Red River water trail identifies access and camping rules, but no station-specific endpoint/threshold package was established for Pembina.
No coordinates, image, or geometry were promoted without a supported gauge-linked route package.

reviews.decisionReason: USGS 05104500 is Roseau River below South Fork near Malung. It is a hydrologic/flood-monitoring station, but the bounded discovery sweep found no official state-water-trail segment or public point-to-point paddling package for this gauge reach. Local Roseau River access references do not establish a route-capable corridor with named endpoints and paddle thresholds.
blockers: No official state-water-trail or manager-backed point-to-point route package found below South Fork near Malung.
No named public endpoint pair, paddling threshold, camping, safety, coordinate, image, or geometry evidence.
Gauge context is hydrologic/flood monitoring rather than a supported paddle route.

reviews.decisionReason: USGS 05106000 is Sprague Creek near Sprague, Manitoba, Canada. The provider inventory places it in the Minnesota district and the state-coverage baseline, but the official station metadata identifies a Canadian location outside the supported Minnesota route geography. It is therefore screened out rather than treated as an eligible Minnesota paddle gauge.
blockers: Station is in Manitoba, Canada, not Minnesota or another currently supported U.S. state.
No supported PaddleToday route geography or state-water-trail package applies to this Canadian station.
evidence: https://waterdata.usgs.gov/monitoring-location/USGS-05106000/ identifies Sprague Creek near Sprague, Manitoba, Canada, at 48.992599, -95.662148 and explicitly lists Country as Canada.

reviews.decisionReason: Bounded official-source screen confirmed current USGS discharge/stage telemetry and multiple public Roseau River accesses, including City Park, Stoies Bridge, Trangsrud, and Caribou. The Roseau River Water Trail proposal identifies Ross Town Hall as a planned site, but no manager-verified paired endpoint package or station-specific paddling threshold/safety/camping/geometry package cleared. Preserve as explicit blocked opportunity.
blockers: The Roseau River Water Trail proposal identifies Ross Town Hall among six planned/significant sites, but does not establish a manager-verified scored endpoint pair or route distance for PaddleToday.
No station-specific paddling threshold or accepted conservative threshold ladder was found for USGS 05107500; current telemetry alone is not a paddleability threshold.
Named public access listings exist, but camping, safety, coordinates, rights-clean image, and canonical geometry evidence for a Ross reach remain incomplete.

reviews.decisionReason: USGS 05112000 is Roseau River below State Ditch 51 near Caribou. No route is published from this stale/unsupported gauge.
blockers: USGS reports no continuous, daily, or field measurement data.

No defensible gauge-tied threshold and public access sequence supports a scored route.

lake/river access, safety, camping, coordinate, geometry, and image package incomplete

reviews.decisionReason: USGS 05292000 is the Minnesota River at Ortonville station and is provider-equivalent to MN DNR gauge 108. The DNR station has already been dispositioned as route-capable but blocked because the Ortonville-to-Marsh Lake segment lacks a strong validated route package; adding a duplicate USGS route would not improve endpoint, threshold, or safety coverage.
blockers: Provider-equivalent to blocked MN DNR gauge 108.
No validated Ortonville corridor route package exists.
Duplicate provider entry would add no endpoint, threshold, or safety value.

reviews.decisionReason: USGS 05293000 is the Yellow Bank River near Odessa, an active stream gauge in an agricultural watershed. The reviewed official sources provide monitoring and watershed context but no Minnesota state-water-trail segment, named public paddling endpoints, route recommendation, or route-specific paddling thresholds for Yellow Bank. It is screened out under the current quality bar rather than promoted from gauge presence alone.
blockers: No official Minnesota state-water-trail route or recommended paddling section was identified.
No named public put-in/take-out pair, camping/access package, or route-specific safety and flow thresholds were identified.
The gauge's current telemetry and imagery establish monitoring value, not a defensible recreational route.
evidence: https://waterdata.usgs.gov/monitoring-location/USGS-05293000/ identifies Yellow Bank River Near Odessa, a current stream gauge with continuous data through 2026-08-14 and a 459-square-mile drainage area.
https://www.dnr.state.mn.us/watertrails/az.html lists Minnesota state water trails and does not list Yellow Bank River.
https://mn.water.usgs.gov/infodata/ann-repts/annrpt00/discontinued.pdf provides historical USGS basin/station context for Yellow Bank River near Odessa but no paddling designation.

reviews.decisionReason: USGS 05294000 is the Pomme de Terre River at Appleton and is provider-equivalent to the covered MN DNR Appleton gauge used by the existing Larson-to-Appleton and Pomme #1-to-Appleton scored routes. Those routes already include the official level ladder, endpoints, camping, hazards, and geometry; a second USGS record would duplicate the same corridor.
blockers: Provider-equivalent to covered MN DNR Appleton gauge 168.
Existing Pomme de Terre routes already carry the full endpoint, threshold, camping, safety, and geometry package.
Duplicate provider record adds no distinct route value.

reviews.decisionReason: Fresh official DNR Map 2 review confirms the Lac qui Parle River confluence at Minnesota River mile 273.5 and nearby lake access, but provides no distinct tributary route segment or endpoint pair tied to USGS 05300000. No station-specific threshold, camping, safety, coordinate, or geometry package cleared; preserve as explicitly blocked.
blockers: No existing scored route explicitly adopts USGS 05300000.

Gauge-specific paddling threshold, endpoint coordinates/geometry, camping/no-camping terms, and tributary hazard package remain unresolved.

reviews.decisionReason: usgs:05304500 is a product-supported direct USGS Chippewa station in a corridor already represented by MN DNR site 24 / Chippewa River near Milan, but no scored route is configured to this USGS provider key. Current coverage gates do not treat cross-provider equivalents as covered, so this remains blocked rather than forcing a duplicate route or silent gauge migration.
blockers: Existing route coverage uses the equivalent MN DNR site 24 / Chippewa River near Milan gauge, not usgs:05304500.
The gauge-coverage gate requires a scored route tied to the reviewed provider key before status can be covered.
No duplicate Chippewa route is justified because the official DNR endpoint, threshold, camping, safety, coordinate, and geometry package is already represented.

Preserve as proxy-only blocked.

reviews.decisionReason: USGS 05311000 is the Minnesota River at Montevideo live discharge/stage station and corresponds to existing scored routes using MN DNR gauge 99. The DNR route package already supplies official thresholds and endpoints; the USGS key is not explicitly adopted, and adding a duplicate USGS-backed route would add no endpoint or safety value.
blockers: Existing scored Montevideo routes use MN DNR gauge 99 rather than USGS 05311000.
Provider-specific USGS threshold adoption and route metadata are not present.
Duplicate USGS route would add no endpoint or safety value.

reviews.decisionReason: USGS 05311150 is a live discharge/stage station at Highway 212 in Granite Falls, directly relevant to the Minnesota River corridor and near the existing War Memorial-to-Kinney scored route. That route currently uses the Montevideo DNR gauge as a proxy; the USGS station could improve direct coverage, but no validated station-specific threshold mapping or product gauge migration has been completed.
blockers: Existing scored War Memorial-to-Kinney route uses a Montevideo DNR proxy rather than USGS 05311150.
USGS station-specific paddling thresholds and trend handling are not yet validated against the route's Granite Falls hazards and portage boundary.
This is a gauge integration/route-quality task, not a reason to add a duplicate route.

reviews.decisionReason: Current USGS telemetry is available through 2026-08-19, but no official Yellow Medicine endpoint pair, station-specific paddling threshold, safety/camping, access, image, coordinates, or geometry package was found. Nearby Minnesota River access does not establish a distinct route. Preserve as explicitly blocked.
blockers: USGS live discharge/stage telemetry exists through 2026-08-19, but no accepted paddling threshold tied to station 05313500 was found.
No official Yellow Medicine point-to-point paddling route or named public endpoint pair was found; nearby Minnesota River route coverage does not establish a Yellow Medicine route.
DNR maps identify the Yellow Medicine confluence and nearby access context, but route-specific geometry, access legality, threshold evidence, safety/camping, and image decisions remain unresolved.

reviews.decisionReason: Fresh official-source screen confirms a route-relevant Redwood River corridor and historical USGS telemetry, but no lawful public endpoint pair near Marshall and no station-specific paddling threshold package. Existing Vesta-to-Wabasso and Wabasso-to-Redwood Lake routes cover the documented lower access corridor; the upper gap is not publishable without a distinct endpoint and accepted gauge guidance.
blockers: Legacy USGS telemetry is available only through 2026-08-01 (latest instantaneous value 36.5 cfs / 7.08 ft); the modern page does not provide a current continuous/daily/field package.

The official Redwood corridor begins near Marshall, but the 2024 Brown/Redwood public-access map lists only Redwood River Vesta and Wabasso accesses; no validated lawful Marshall-area endpoint pair was found.
No accepted station-specific paddling threshold, upper-reach camping/safety package, endpoint coordinates, rights-clean image, or canonical geometry package cleared.

reviews.decisionReason: USGS 05316500 near Redwood Falls is provider-equivalent to the existing MN DNR Redwood Falls gauge 196 used by the scored Redwood River Vesta-to-Wabasso route. The existing route already has official DNR thresholds, public endpoints, camping/safety context, coordinates, and geometry; adding a duplicate USGS route would add no endpoint or safety value and provider-specific duplicate coverage is not counted as covered under the completeness policy.
blockers: Existing scored Redwood route uses equivalent MN DNR gauge 196.
USGS duplicate would add no distinct endpoint, threshold, camping, safety, or geometry value.
Provider-specific USGS route metadata is not present and is not justified as a duplicate package.

reviews.decisionReason: The gauge appears only as fallback or proxy evidence and needs a direct-corridor disposition.

USGS 05316770 is recorded as the direct live gauge for the New Ulm Minnesota River scored corridor in the route inventory; the station has current discharge and stage telemetry, and the route package carries the required official water-trail and access evidence.

USGS 05317000 is a direct Cottonwood discharge station near New Ulm, but existing scored Cottonwood routes use equivalent MN DNR Leavenworth/New Ulm gauges and current coverage gates do not silently count cross-provider equivalents or justify duplicate route packages.
blockers: No scored route is configured to the USGS provider key.
Cross-provider DNR equivalence is not counted as covered without explicit route-package migration.

reviews.decisionReason: USGS 05317200 is a live discharge and stage station on the Little Cottonwood River near Courtland. Minnesota DNR maps show the Little Cottonwood confluence and Courtland access on the Minnesota River State Water Trail, but do not identify a Little Cottonwood paddling section or route-specific gauge interpretation; no PaddleToday route corridor was found.
blockers: No official Little Cottonwood State Water Trail or recommended paddling section found.
DNR material identifies the tributary confluence but does not establish a route package or gauge interpretation for the tributary.
No named Little Cottonwood endpoint sequence, threshold, camping, safety, or geometry package was found.

evidence.label: USGS Little Cottonwood River near Courtland
evidence.note: USGS provides live discharge and stage observations for the tributary station.

evidence.label: Minnesota DNR Cottonwood and Minnesota River map
evidence.note: Official map places Courtland access and the Little Cottonwood confluence on the Minnesota River trail, without a Little Cottonwood route section.

evidence.label: Minnesota DNR Cottonwood River trail
evidence.note: Official trail page describes the supported Cottonwood River corridor, not the Little Cottonwood tributary gauge reach.

reviews.decisionReason: USGS 05319500 is a current Watonwan River station near Garden City on an official 30-mile Minnesota DNR paddling corridor. Existing scored Watonwan routes already use the co-located Minnesota DNR Garden City interpreted gauge (site 254), but no current route directly uses the USGS provider key. Keep the provider-equivalent station blocked rather than duplicating a route; a future review can promote it only if the product deliberately supports USGS as a distinct direct source with matching thresholds and evidence.
blockers: Existing scored Watonwan routes use the co-located MN DNR site 254; the USGS station is a provider-equivalent duplicate, not a distinct reach signal.
The product does not currently define a direct USGS threshold model for this corridor, so assigning the DNR interpretation to a different provider would be an unsupported substitution.
Do not create another route solely to increase provider-key coverage.
evidence: https://waterdata.usgs.gov/monitoring-location/USGS-05319500/ identifies the current Watonwan River Near Garden City stream station and shows continuous data through 2026-08-14.
https://www.dnr.state.mn.us/state-water-trails/watonwan-river/segments-maps.html documents the official 30-mile Madelia-to-Garden-City paddling corridor, calm-to-quick flows, and snag hazards.
https://www.dnr.state.mn.us/river_levels/index.html is the official DNR interpreted source used by the existing Watonwan route cards.

reviews.decisionReason: Fresh USGS and Minnesota DNR review confirms the Rapidan-area gauge remains live, but the official Blue Earth trail map marks RM 10.0-2.8 as unsafe after the dam failure because of debris, unstable channel, and recirculating currents. The DNR's supported day trip begins downstream at County Road 90 and uses a different reach relationship; no safe new endpoint package can be tied to this gauge. Preserve the durable block unless a manager publishes a safe, supported reach and gauge relationship.
blockers: Minnesota DNR Blue Earth map marks the Rapidan Dam failure area as unsafe, with debris, unstable channel, and recirculating currents; paddling through the dam area is not recommended.
Existing scored Blue Earth route support begins downstream at County Road 90 Bridge to Sibley Park and does not use this Rapidan-area gauge as the route's direct condition source.
No safe public endpoint package or route-specific threshold relationship was established for the gauge reach adjacent to the failed dam.
evidence: https://waterdata.usgs.gov/monitoring-location/05320000/ identifies BLUE EARTH RIVER NEAR RAPIDAN, MN.
https://files.dnr.state.mn.us/maps/canoe_routes/blueearth.pdf marks the Rapidan Dam failure area (RM 10.0-2.8) as dangerous and not recommended for paddling.
https://files.dnr.state.mn.us/maps/canoe_routes/blueearth.pdf names the supported County Road 90 Bridge to Sibley Park recommended section downstream of the dam area.
https://www.dnr.state.mn.us/state-water-trails/blue-earth-river/index.html confirms the Blue Earth River State Water Trail.

reviews.decisionReason: Fresh official DNR map review confirms the Rapidan area has a dangerous recirculating current/debris hazard and only a Blue Earth River package downstream of the dam; no distinct Le Sueur endpoint pair or station-specific threshold/safety package tied to USGS 05320500 cleared. Preserve as explicitly blocked.
blockers: No existing scored route explicitly adopts USGS 05320500.
DNR explicitly warns to stay clear of the dangerous recirculating current below Rapidan Dam and flags the dam/failure debris hazard.

reviews.decisionReason: Fresh USGS, Minnesota DNR, and NPS review confirms robust live telemetry and a genuine lower Dakota County paddling corridor, including an NPS boat ramp with GPS. However, DNR's named parcels are primarily access/fishing sites with a private-property warning, NPS describes a braided maze of often dead-end channels, and partners are still working to expand access and secure official water-trail designation. No lawful station-tied endpoint pair or route-specific threshold clears the route bar; preserve as an explicit no-add and do not conflate with the unrelated northern Vermilion State Water Trail.
blockers: No named public put-in/take-out pair or DNR recommended paddling section tied to the Empire gauge was identified.
DNR lists fishing/access parcels and warns that property north of 200th Street is private; launch suitability and a lawful station-specific endpoint pair remain unconfirmed.
NPS describes a braided floodplain maze with often dead-end channels and says partners are still working to expand canoe/kayak access and secure official water-trail designation.
No authoritative route-specific numeric threshold was identified despite live USGS discharge, stage, and stream-level telemetry.
evidence: https://waterdata.usgs.gov/nwis/uv?legacy=1&site_no=05345000 identifies USGS 05345000 near Empire and reports discharge, gage height, and stream-level telemetry through 2026-07-16.

https://www.dnr.state.mn.us/areas/fisheries/eastmetro/troutstreams/vermillion.html identifies the Dakota County Vermillion River and lists Rambling River Park, Miles parcel, Kamen unit, and Otting parcel access locations.

https://www.nps.gov/miss/planyourvisit/vermrive.htm notes that paddlers and partners are still working to expand canoe/kayak access and secure official water-trail designation for this lower Vermillion corridor.
https://www.dnr.state.mn.us/state-water-trails/vermilion-river/index.html documents a separate northern Vermilion River State Water Trail and must not be conflated with the Empire station.

reviews.decisionReason: USGS 05353800 is the Straight River near Faribault and sits on the same official water-trail corridor as the existing Straight River routes. The authoritative USGS monitoring page currently reports continuous data only through 2026-08-04 and daily data through 2026-08-02, so it is not a dependable current live-gauge source for a new route package. The existing cards already use the Minnesota DNR interpreted Faribault gauge (site 247), so this duplicate provider station is recorded as stale_or_unsupported rather than used to create another route.
blockers: USGS monitoring metadata shows the latest continuous data ending 2026-08-04 and latest daily data ending 2026-08-02, which is stale for current trip decisions.
No separate route package should be created when the supported DNR interpreted Faribault gauge already covers the corridor.
Reconsider only if USGS telemetry resumes and supplies a distinct, useful reach signal beyond the DNR gauge.
evidence: https://waterdata.usgs.gov/monitoring-location/USGS-05353800/ identifies Straight River Near Faribault, MN, with continuous data through 2026-08-04 and daily data through 2026-08-02.
https://www.dnr.state.mn.us/state-water-trails/straight-river/segments-maps.html documents the official Straight River paddling corridor and seasonal hazards.
https://www.dnr.state.mn.us/river_levels/index.html is the supported Minnesota DNR interpreted river-level source used by existing route cards.

reviews.decisionReason: Fast evidence screen confirmed a real Cannon River corridor and exact County Road 29 access, but Minnesota DNR's official interpretation for this gauge is qualitative only. Available numeric guidance is either percentile context or tied to the separate Northfield gauge, so no defensible station-specific threshold or conversion cleared the scored-route gate. Preserve as a durable no-add.
At least one scored route uses this gauge directly.
Chub Creek telemetry is a small tributary monitoring site, not a Minnesota DNR state-water-trail gauge or supported point-to-point paddling corridor; no route-capable package was found.
blockers: No official state water-trail segment or public paddling endpoint package surfaced for Chub Creek.
Gage-height telemetry alone does not establish paddle relevance.

reviews.decisionReason: USGS 05355080 is Prairie Creek near Cannon Falls, but the current USGS station page states that no continuous, daily, or field measurement data are available and that the site is crest-stage record only. Cannon Falls paddling routes use the Cannon River corridor and its supported gauge family, not this unsupported Prairie Creek station.
blockers: USGS reports no continuous, daily, or field measurements.
Crest-stage-only data cannot support a live PaddleToday gauge.
No distinct Prairie Creek state-water-trail route package is established.

reviews.decisionReason: Same-corridor duplicate of MN DNR 345 at Cannon 9th Street. Official USGS telemetry and DNR Cannon mapping were verified, but no distinct endpoint pair or defensible station-specific threshold package exists beyond the already scored Cannon corridor. Preserve as a provider-integration gap rather than create a duplicate route.
blockers: No defensible route-specific low/ideal/high threshold band is published for USGS 05355092.
Existing route packages rely on official MN DNR Welch interpretation bands; substituting raw 9th Street discharge without a validated conversion would weaken safety evidence.

evidence.note: USGS provides live discharge, gage height, and stream-level telemetry at the Cannon 9th Street bridge.
DNR Cannon Map 2 places the station in the lower-Cannon route corridor near Riverside and Miesville access points.
Official interpreted Cannon thresholds are published for the Welch station, not for the USGS 9th Street station.

reviews.decisionReason: At least one scored route uses this gauge directly.

Bounded official-source screen reconfirmed live USGS discharge/stage at Red Wing (6,770 cfs and 2.06 ft on 2026-08-24), public Pool 3 access, and named Red Wing-area access points. USACE publishes Lock and Dam 3 navigation thresholds, but those are lock/outdraft thresholds rather than a paddling ladder; DNR documents lock/dam, channel, wake, backwater, seasonal, and camping/property constraints without a route-specific go/no-go band or complete paired endpoint/geometry package. Durable no-add; preserve as explicitly blocked.
blockers: Named Red Wing-area public accesses exist, but no paired endpoint/geometry package is validated for a distinct gauge-linked reach.
USACE Lock and Dam 3 thresholds are navigation/outdraft thresholds, not a station-specific paddling ladder.
Lock and Dam 3, navigation traffic, wakes, backwater, seasonal restrictions, and shoreline/property conditions require dedicated route handling.
DNR access sources do not establish a route-specific camping, image, geometry, or conservative paddling go/no-go package.

reviews.decisionReason: The Chippewa River at Bishops Bridge is a regulated large river with historical USGS records, but the current monitoring-location page reports no available continuous/daily/field data and no current PaddleToday route package was found for this gauge reach. Treat it as unsupported until current data and route evidence are refreshed.
At least one scored route uses this gauge directly.

Intentional no-add: the current USGS monitoring page reports no continuous, daily, or field measurement data for 05357335, so the station cannot support a product live-gauge operating band. No complete Bear River endpoint, threshold, access, camping, safety, image, and geometry package was found.
At least one scored route uses this gauge directly.
A route candidate references this gauge but does not clear scored-route publication.

Bounded research found a strong gauge-matched North Fork Yellow River novice reach from Yellow River Road to CTH M: American Whitewater gives 9.4 miles, Class I-II, a direct gauge at the put-in, marked rapids, and a gauge observation around 85 cfs that floated a three-person canoe. Iowa DNR sources describe Waterloo Creek as trout stream and wildlife-area habitat; the bounded review found no Iowa water-trail listing, named canoe/kayak route, public point-to-point endpoint pair, route thresholds, camping/access package, image decision, or gauge-linked geometry for this creek. Screen it out rather than infer a paddle product from a trout-stream gauge.
blockers: Stage-only trout-stream telemetry does not provide a scored paddling threshold model.
No Iowa DNR water-trail or public point-to-point paddling endpoint package surfaced for Waterloo Creek.
No route camping, safety, image, coordinate, or geometry package exists for this creek gauge.

USGS 05389400 is Bloody Run Creek near Marquette. Iowa DNR and county sources describe a short, coldwater trout stream with fishing, habitat, camping, and water-quality protections, but no named canoe/kayak route or point-to-point paddling corridor at the gauge. Treat it as fishing/conservation water rather than infer a paddle route from streamflow data.
blockers: No named canoe/kayak route or point-to-point paddling corridor was found in Iowa DNR water-trail sources.
Official sources characterize the 6.5-mile reach primarily as trout habitat/fishing and camping, not a scored paddling product.
No route-specific threshold, endpoints, safety, image, or river-line geometry package exists.

Wisconsin DNR describes the Little Plover River reach primarily as a brook-trout wade-fishing area that can dry up seasonally; the nearby Springville Pond carry-in access is a separate impoundment and does not establish a route on this gauge reach.

USGS 05400760 is a live discharge and stage gauge on a genuinely paddle-relevant Wisconsin River reach between Biron and Nekoosa. Public access is documented at Ben Hanson Park and the Wisconsin River Trips segment identifies launch/take-out options, but the station-specific threshold interpretation, complete paired endpoint package, camping terms, hazard/portage treatment, and verified river-line geometry are not yet assembled to the product quality bar. Keep the gauge route-capable but blocked rather than publishing a speculative scored route.

Big Roche a Cri Creek is a small 15.7-square-mile creek monitoring site at County Highway G near Leola. USGS telemetry is available, but no public point-to-point paddle corridor or complete route package was found; watershed/flood documentation does not establish a recreational route.

Bounded research completed with no route added. Wisconsin River Trips supplies a useful 80 cfs / 2.5 ft reference for a Yellow River reach and official Wisconsin sources confirm Dexter County Park, the Yellow River Floodplain Forest, and canoe access. However, Dexter Dam releases create station-to-reach variability, the selected Highway 54-to-Highway 80 corridor lacks a fully verified public endpoint pair and arrival offsets, and safety/geometry/image evidence is incomplete. Keep blocked rather than treating the reference as universally valid.
blockers: Dexter Dam releases create station-to-reach variability and the 80 cfs reference is not validated for every selected reach.

reviews.decisionReason: Bounded route research confirmed a real Yellow River corridor below Necedah Dam with public fishing access and a Buckhorn State Park takeout, plus a direct USGS discharge/stage gauge. However, current route evidence reports severe and changing logjam conditions, swift current and deadfalls, open-water wind exposure, and a flowage section with little current. The only numeric paddling guidance found is an informal 90 cfs observation rather than an authoritative station-specific threshold; no complete canonical geometry, arrival offsets, camping terms, or rights-clean image package cleared publication. No speculative route was added.
blockers: Current reports describe numerous or changing logjams, swift current/deadfalls, and stronger hazard at higher flows; no manager-backed clearance or safety package is validated.
The 90 cfs paddling observation is informal and not an authoritative station-specific threshold for this gauge.
Public endpoints are plausible, but selected endpoint coordinates, arrival offsets, canonical river-line geometry, camping terms, and rights-clean image decision remain incomplete.

reviews.decisionReason: Fresh review confirms Emmet County and Iowa DNR document a distinct West Fork Des Moines water trail from the Estherville North Trailhead to the 4th Street Bridge, with additional School Creek and downstream access, a dam portage, and flood/drought cautions. USGS 05476500 has live stage telemetry but current discharge is not available (historical discharge ended in 2011). The route remains blocked because no defensible stage-to-paddling threshold or complete station-linked coordinate/geometry and camping/image package is sourced; no route added.
blockers: Current station is stage-only; a defensible stage-to-paddling threshold model is unresolved.
